faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children at home in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, when the subjects and year groups are close enough that one person genuinely covers both. Back-to-back sibling sessions work well for MYP Maths and Science, or for two children both in early IGCSE, and they save a travel trip and an evening. They stop working once one child reaches DP1 or Year 11, because the component knowledge required diverges and you end up with a specialist for one child and a compromise for the other. Where the subjects do not allow it, the usual answer is one tutor at home for the younger child and an online specialist for the elder in a different room.

faqs.question: My elder child's tutor was excellent. Why would they not suit my younger one?
faqs.answer: Because fit is between one tutor's way of explaining and one child's way of getting stuck, and siblings get stuck differently. A tutor who was patient and structured can be exactly wrong for a quick child who needs pushing, and a demanding tutor who turned around a drifting DP2 student can flatten a nervous Year 9. The year group matters as much as the personality: someone outstanding on DP Maths HL may not have taught MYP in years. Try them if you want, but treat the first session as a real diagnostic rather than a formality, and be willing to change.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on when two children are studying?
faqs.answer: They depend on board and level, subject scarcity, travel distance, session length and frequency, and when in the year you book. We do not publish a price list, because an honest one would need all of those variables. With two children, the saving that actually exists comes from shared logistics rather than a bulk rate: one tutor travelling once for two back-to-back sessions, both children on the same evening, and a tutor whose own commute is short. Cross-city matches cost more and hold worse. Booking in May or June, when exam-year demand has cleared, usually gives you more choice than booking in November.

faqs.question: How do records get handed over when we change tutors between years?
faqs.answer: Ask the outgoing tutor for a closing note and keep it with your child's reports. It should list topics covered, past papers attempted with dates, the errors that kept recurring, what was deliberately left undone, and where the child stands with their own school teacher. We ask for this whenever a tutor finishes or is replaced, and we pass it to the incoming tutor with your permission. A new tutor who reads that note starts from a real position in the first session instead of spending two weeks rediscovering it, and the same note is useful again when a younger sibling reaches that year.

faqs.question: We live in Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road. Will a tutor come on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is based in Thane rather than travelling from Mumbai's western suburbs. Ghodbunder Road decides this: a tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali quickly off-peak and slowly in the evening peak, and a tutor coming from Borivali or Mulund will quietly start arriving late by the second month. We match Thane households to Thane tutors, with Mulund tutors as the occasional exception on the Eastern Express Highway side. For a scarce DP subject where no local specialist exists, online is the arrangement that survives the monsoon, and most families here end up hybrid.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: At four weeks you should be looking for process rather than marks, so check that first. Is homework being started earlier, are past papers being attempted under time, can the child say what a question is asking before answering it? If none of that has changed, raise it with the tutor directly and ask what they think the actual break is. If the answer is vague or still the same as the first session, change the tutor. Marks move on school assessments over a term, not a month, but the underlying habits should visibly shift inside four weeks.

faqs.question: Does online actually work for the younger child while the elder has home sessions?
faqs.answer: It works for the elder child far more reliably than for the younger one, so run it the other way round. Online suits abstract DP material, marked-draft review and doubt clearing, where screen sharing is genuinely efficient. A child in MYP or early IGCSE leaks attention inside twenty minutes online and nobody sees the phone under the desk. If your timetable forces the younger child onto a screen, keep them in the room with the open door, sit within earshot for the first fortnight, and treat the arrangement as temporary rather than the plan.

faqs.question: Should we keep the same tutor when our child moves from MYP 5 into DP1?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the test is whether that tutor can tell your child a draft is not good enough yet. DP asks for independent written work and a tolerance for hard feedback that the MYP years did not. A tutor who has been encouraging since Year 7 often cannot switch register, and the child cannot hear it from them. If sessions are comfortable and nothing is improving between them, that is the signal. Keeping continuity through MYP is usually right; carrying it into DP1 unexamined is the most common expensive mistake families make with a second or third child.

faqs.question: What if a tutor is not working out for one child but is fine for the other?
faqs.answer: Change the one and leave the other alone. Tell us specifically what is failing: work not being done, explanations not landing, the slot drifting, strong content but weak exam technique. We ask the outgoing tutor for a closing note, shortlist again against what you have just learned, and keep the second child's arrangement exactly as it is. Families often assume both children must move together out of fairness, which usually breaks the arrangement that was working. Two children are two separate matches that happen to share an address and an evening.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home for both children's sessions?
faqs.answer: For the younger child, yes, at least for the first few weeks; for an older student, not usually. Home sessions supervise themselves when an adult is somewhere in the flat, and that is most of their value over online. What actually needs a parent is the five-minute debrief afterwards, which is where you learn whether the hour did anything. Where both parents work late, the common arrangement is a session that ends before you get home and a short tutor message the same evening, with one session a week deliberately scheduled when someone is in.

faqs.question: My children are on different boards, one IGCSE and one IB DP. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost always yes once the elder child is in DP. Running IB home tuitions in Mumbai for two children on different boards means working two curricula in parallel, with different assessment language, different internal assessment shapes and different deadline calendars. One strong generalist genuinely covers both children at MYP 2 and MYP 3 level. Beyond Year 10 the components diverge too far: a tutor spending the fortnight on an IA sign-off cannot also drill IGCSE mole calculations. Keep the shared evening and the shared corridor if you can, and accept two people.

sections.heading: How a fees question becomes a shortlist of home tutors in Mumbai
paragraphs: A parent who writes in asking about IB home tutor fees in Mumbai usually expects a number to come back. What comes back instead is a short list of questions, because a quote offered before anyone knows the subject, the level, the address and the hour is a guess with a confident tone. Parents often ask for the best IB tutor in Mumbai and a fee in the same sentence, and both questions have the same answer: it depends entirely on the request. The request that produces a usable quote names the programme and the year, the exact subject and route, the assessment that is closest, the building and the suburb, and the two or three evening slots that would genuinely work in that household.

The shortlist comes out of those answers rather than a rate card. A Diploma Programme (DP) Year 2 student in Worli sitting the May session with a Physics Internal Assessment (IA) draft due needs someone who has marked that component against the current criteria, and the pool of people who have is thinner than the pool who can teach the syllabus well. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) Year 4 student in Kandivali East who needs her Maths confidence rebuilt draws on a far wider pool. Two requests, two shortlists, two sets of quotes, and none of them comparable with each other.

The sequence is deliberately unexciting, and it runs in the same order whether the request comes from Cuffe Parade or Kharghar. Nothing is quoted until the third step, because the first two steps are what make the third one mean anything. If a platform or an agency hands you a figure before it has asked where you live and what your child is being assessed on next month, that figure is a marketing number rather than a quote, and it will be revised the moment reality arrives.

At the introduction stage you speak to the tutor directly before any money moves. That conversation is where the scope gets written down: how long a session runs, what happens between sessions, whether marking and written feedback sit inside the quote, how travel is treated, and what notice either side gives. IB Gram keeps that summary on the record so that a disagreement in week six has something to refer back to instead of two different memories of one phone call.

sections.heading: Why does a DP Higher Level quote in Mumbai differ from an MYP one?
paragraphs: Because the work behind the session is different, not because the hour is longer. A Diploma Programme (DP) Higher Level (HL) tutor in Mumbai is marking Paper 3 style questions, reading Internal Assessment (IA) drafts against published criteria and tracking a predicted grade that universities will eventually see. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) tutor is teaching criteria A to D and building working habits. The second job is valuable; the first carries more unpaid hours stacked around it.

Within the International Baccalaureate (IB), each tier changes the preparation load in a way that shows up in what a tutor asks for. Primary Years Programme (PYP) support is mostly in-session: a tutor arrives, works through number sense or reading fluency, and leaves. The Middle Years Programme adds criterion-referenced tasks and the personal project in Year 5. The Diploma Programme adds six subjects, Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and an Internal Assessment in almost every subject, each with its own deadline. A DP2 tutor is effectively on call through January and February and quotes with that month in mind.

The Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel side splits differently. An International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) student choosing between Core and Extended Mathematics, or between the single-award and double-award science routes, needs a tutor who knows which paper combination that school enters students for, because teaching the wrong tier wastes a term nobody gets back. AS and A Level work sits closer to Diploma Programme HL in preparation load than to MYP. IB Gram matches across all IB and IGCSE subjects and the whole span of IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor requests in Mumbai.

None of this gives you a figure, and it is not meant to. It gives you a reason to ask a question when a DP Higher Level Chemistry quote and an MYP Year 3 Mathematics quote arrive at the same amount from the same person. Either the Higher Level work is being under-scoped or the MYP work is being over-scoped, and a tutor who cannot explain why the two are identical has not thought about either of them properly.

sections.heading: The thin-pool subjects in Mumbai, and what a small tutor pool does to a quote
paragraphs: Subject scarcity is the lever parents underestimate most. IB Gram lists all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai can be matched for, but the pools behind those subject names are uneven. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches (AA) at Higher Level, Physics HL, Chemistry HL and the less commonly taught Language B options sit in thin pools across the city. Business Management, Economics at Standard Level (SL), English A Language and Literature, and MYP Mathematics sit in deep ones. A thin pool means fewer people can take a 7pm weekday slot, and the people who can take it are aware of that.

Depth of experience matters as much as breadth of coverage. A Mathematics AA HL tutor has to be comfortable with Paper 3, the long investigative paper, and with an Exploration the student has usually scoped badly on the first attempt. A Chemistry HL tutor is marking an Internal Assessment built on an experiment the student ran once in a school laboratory and cannot repeat. An Economics tutor is reading commentaries against a rubric that rewards specific diagrammatic work and penalises vague evaluation. Each of those is marking time spent between sessions, and the honest quotes say so instead of pretending the work fits inside the hour.

Languages behave differently again. A Spanish Language B HL student in Juhu needs oral practice, which means a tutor whose spoken Spanish is strong enough to run a mock individual oral, and that narrows the Mumbai pool sharply. Hindi B and French B are easier to staff at every level. On the Cambridge side, First Language English and Mathematics are everywhere, while Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and Music are not. A parent looking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai households commonly need will get a same-week answer for some subjects and a wait for others.

The practical move is to ask what a tutor has actually marked rather than what they can teach. The question that separates two candidates is narrow: which components of this subject have you assessed against the current criteria, and in which examination session? A tutor who answers with specifics is quoting from experience and can tell you where the marks leak. A tutor who answers with a general statement about loving the subject is quoting from hope, and hope is the most expensive thing on this page.

sections.heading: Travel time and the contested evening slot across Mumbai's six zones
paragraphs: Geography enters a quote twice, once as distance and once as the hour. A tutor in Mumbai, Maharashtra gives up an evening rather than an hour, and the part of the evening they give up is invisible to the family at the table. IB home tutor fees in Mumbai therefore move by zone for reasons that have nothing to do with what a zone can afford. South Mumbai is short-distance and slow: Worli to Colaba is a modest hop that the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals can stretch past forty minutes in the evening peak. Tutors are matched inside the island, between Cuffe Parade, Fort, Walkeshwar and Napean Sea Road, served by the Western Line out of Churchgate, the Harbour Line and now the Coastal Road.

The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, so a tutor moving from Bandra West to Khar West or Santacruz West travels easily, and the same tutor sent from Juhu to Kandivali East at six in the evening does not. Matching along the line works; matching across it does not. Metro Line 1 lets an Andheri West tutor reach Ghatkopar, Metro Lines 2A and 7 have changed the Dahisar and Borivali picture, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link makes a Malad West tutor workable in Worli on a Saturday morning and nowhere near workable on a Tuesday at seven.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai is the exception that shapes every quote there: it has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar East, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road is what makes a Kurla match viable at all. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West, and the Eastern Freeway makes a Chembur tutor reachable from Wadala and the island far faster than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, and tutors are matched node to node: Vashi to Sanpada, Nerul to Seawoods, CBD Belapur across to Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway. The Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line have shortened the crossing, but pulling a tutor off the island for a weekday evening slot in Kharghar still rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and Ghodbunder sets the schedule: Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes from the station off-peak and close to an hour at seven.

sections.heading: Which months push Mumbai families into a second weekly session?
paragraphs: January and February, and then April into the May session. That is when Mumbai families add a second weekly slot, and the second slot is the largest single change most households ever make to what they spend on tutoring. At Dhirubhai Ambani International School, Oberoi International School and Ecole Mondiale World School the Diploma Programme internal deadlines cluster inside that window, and a good tutor's diary fills accordingly by December.

The calendar itself is reasonably predictable. Mumbai schools run June starts, so Diploma Programme Year 1 begins in June and the first real assessment pressure arrives around November. Internal Assessment drafts in the sciences and Mathematics land in the DP2 winter, the Extended Essay final submission sits just before or just after the December break depending on the school, and the Theory of Knowledge essay deadline usually falls in the same fortnight as at least one Internal Assessment. Cambridge candidates at Cathedral and John Connon School or B.D. Somani International School face mocks in December and January and the main series after that.

Monsoon matters more than parents expect, and it belongs in a fee conversation rather than a weather conversation. From June to September an evening journey across Ghodbunder Road in Thane or along the Western Express Highway can double, and a tutor who committed to a 7pm slot in Kasarvadavali may simply not arrive. Families who plan a term ahead often write a monsoon rule into the arrangement: one online session permitted each month without renegotiating anything. That single line prevents most of the arguments that happen in July and most of the sessions quietly lost in August.

IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named on this page. Naming a school here means only that families in that neighbourhood attend it and that its calendar sets the local pressure points. A tutor who has worked with students from Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane or NES International School in Mulund West knows roughly when the mocks fall and plans the weeks before them; that is useful, and it is the only claim being made.

sections.heading: Does the quote change when an IB online tutor in Mumbai replaces home classes?
paragraphs: Usually yes, and the reason is travel rather than teaching. Home tuition is IB Gram's lead service in Mumbai because a tutor at the dining table sees the handwriting, the missing diagrams, the working skipped in the margin and the phone lying face down beside the notebook. That same tutor also spends an hour of their evening on the Western Express Highway or the Harbour Line, and that hour is real whether or not anybody bills it.

Home classes hold a schedule together in a way online rarely manages. A standing weekly slot in a Bandra West flat or a Hiranandani Gardens tower becomes part of the week, and a student cannot drift off to another tab while someone is sitting beside them. The trade-off is reach. The best-matched Mathematics AA HL tutor for a student in Panvel may live in Andheri West, and asking that person to cross the creek twice a week for a full term is exactly how arrangements collapse in month three. Online keeps the match and loses the table.

Hybrid is what most families in Mumbai settle on without ever naming it. One home session a week for the work that needs a shared page, and one online session for question practice, past paper walkthroughs and the sort of check-in that takes half an hour and could never justify a journey from Mulund West to Nerul. In exam term the online session is usually the one that gets added, because it can sit at an hour no travelling tutor could offer. All IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes Mumbai parents book can be run on this split.

The honest comparison is not home against online on an hourly basis. It is the total cost of an arrangement set against whether it survives a term. An online arrangement that runs for twelve straight weeks does more for a DP2 student than a home arrangement that lapses in week five because the tutor could not keep crossing Mumbai at 7pm. Ask any tutor which mode they can genuinely sustain through both the monsoon and the exam term, and take the answer seriously.

Online keeps the best-matched tutor when the journey is unreasonable

sections.heading: What IB Gram checks in Mumbai before you agree to a weekly slot
paragraphs: Verification is what makes a quote worth reading at all. Before a tutor reaches a shortlist, IB Gram confirms identity against a government photographic document, confirms the degree claimed, and asks for evidence of the board work asserted: which syllabus, which components, which examination sessions. A tutor who says they teach Diploma Programme Chemistry is asked which Internal Assessment criteria they have marked against and when. IB home tutor fees in Mumbai mean very little if the person quoting has not been checked at that level.

There is a second layer that matters more for home tuition than for online work. A tutor entering a residential building in Mumbai is entering a family's home on a weekday evening, so the match is made with gate protocol in mind: the society visitor register, the photo pass that towers in Powai and Thane West routinely require, and whether the building will allow a standing entry for a recurring slot. IB Gram does not control a society's rules and cannot change them; it makes sure the tutor knows them before the first visit instead of discovering them at the gate.

What you should check yourself is narrower and more useful than anything a profile contains. Ask for the tutor's own account of a student they took through the same component, including what went wrong in the middle. Ask them to mark one page of your child's existing work in front of you during the introduction, which takes ten minutes and tells you more than any credential. Ask whether the quote changes if a session runs over. And ask whether they currently teach the same subject at a school full time, because a school teacher's availability collapses in exactly the month you need it most.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and a verified tutor is not a promise of a particular result. Verification removes one category of risk, which is the risk of paying someone who is not who they said they were. The remaining risk is fit, and fit is tested in the first four weeks by watching the work rather than by rereading a profile. An IB private tutor Mumbai families hire with none of these checks done is a gamble with a term of school attached to it.

sections.heading: What moves IB home tutor fees in Mumbai, and how do you compare two quotes?
paragraphs: Six things move a quote, and they move it independently of each other. The programme and level, because Diploma Programme Higher Level work carries marking that Middle Years Programme work does not. Subject scarcity, because the pool for Mathematics AA HL or a less common Language B is small and small pools behave like small pools. Travel distance and journey time, because a tutor crossing from Chembur to Bandra West surrenders more of the evening than one walking across Hiranandani Gardens. Session length and frequency, because two shorter sessions cost a tutor two journeys. Whether it is one student or a pair sharing the table. And demand at the hour you want, because the 7pm weekday slot is contested right across the city.

That is why two quotes for the same subject are rarely the same product. One tutor may be quoting for contact time only: they arrive, they teach, they leave, and anything your child sends afterwards goes unread until the next visit. Another may be quoting for contact time plus marking of a past paper between sessions, written feedback specific enough to act on, a short monthly update to you, and printed practice material. Those two arrangements can look like the same hour quoted differently when they are not the same hour at all, and the difference is invisible unless somebody asks.

A quote becomes comparable the moment you ask a fixed set of questions and write the answers side by side. What exactly is included in a session. Is marking of work between sessions inside the quote or billed separately. Is travel time charged, and does that change if the slot moves later. What happens if we cancel. What happens if you cancel. How much notice does each side give, and is the notice the same in both directions. How and when is payment made, and covering what period. Ask all seven of every tutor on your shortlist and IB home tuition fees in Mumbai stop being a mystery: the thinner quote usually turns out to be the thinner service, and occasionally it turns out to be the better one.

Paying a full term in advance is the single place a fee conversation goes genuinely wrong. The money has gone, the leverage has gone, and if the match is wrong in week three you are arguing about a refund instead of arranging a replacement. Ask instead for a short cycle either side can walk away from: four sessions, reviewed, then renewed if it is working. And budget for the things nobody quotes, because they are what actually surprises families. Past paper packs, a revision guide and printing. The second weekly session that appears in exam term. The younger sibling who watches the arrangement working and wants one too, usually in a different subject with a different tutor.

sections.heading: When to review, what to expect, and what no tutor in Mumbai can promise
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for a grade to move. You are looking for three things: your child can start a question without being told how to start it, the tutor can tell you specifically what is weak rather than generally how it is going, and the work coming back repeats fewer of the same errors. At one term you should see a shift in school assessments and a draft that needed fewer rounds of correction. At one exam cycle you find out whether the predicted grade moved. Anything faster than that is noise, and anyone selling you faster than that is selling.

The honest limit is worth stating plainly rather than burying. IB Gram cannot guarantee grades, and neither can a tutor who has marked Diploma Programme Physics for a decade. What a working arrangement changes is the quality and the quantity of deliberate practice between today and the examination, and that is the only variable anyone in this chain controls. A student who does not open the subject between sessions will not improve regardless of who sits at the table, how carefully the tutor was verified, or what the arrangement cost.

Which leads to the least intuitive sentence on this page. The cheapest arrangement is not the one with the lowest hourly rate. It is the one that ends soonest because it worked. A tutor who fixes a DP2 student's Mathematics AA HL Exploration approach in six sessions has cost that household less than one who provides pleasant and inconclusive company for three terms, whatever the two hourly rates happened to be. So ask every tutor at the introduction what the exit looks like: what has to be true before your child stops needing them, and how you will both recognise it.

When a match is not working, say so in week three instead of week ten. Tell IB Gram what specifically is wrong: the pace, the explanation style, a tutor arriving late off the Eastern Express Highway twice running, a personality mismatch nobody could have predicted from a profile. A replacement is arranged from the same verified pool, and the incoming tutor is briefed on what has already been covered so that the family is not paying twice for the same four weeks of diagnosis.
bullets: Four weeks: fewer repeated errors and a tutor who can name the weakness
One term: a shift in school assessments and fewer draft rounds
One exam cycle: whether the predicted grade actually moved

sections.heading: What to prepare before the first home tuition session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Three things on the table before the tutor arrives: the last two pieces of marked school work with the teacher's comments still on them, the subject guide or syllabus the school is following, and the assessment calendar for this term. A parent who hands those over in the first ten minutes saves an entire session of diagnosis, which is a session paid for either way. If your building in Powai or Thane West needs a visitor pass logged in advance, arrange it the day before rather than letting the tutor wait at the gate while the slot burns away.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel diagnostic. A good tutor spends part of it watching your child attempt a question unaided, because what a student does when stuck is the entire diagnosis and nothing else reveals it. By the end you should have a specific statement of what is weak, a plan for the next four sessions, and one clear sentence about what will happen between sessions and who is responsible for it. If the first session is a lecture delivered at your child, that is a signal worth acting on early.

Agree the administrative part before session two rather than after a disagreement. Session length, the standing slot and the fallback slot, who confirms a change and by when, how marking between sessions is handled, the notice each side gives, and the payment cycle. Keep it short and keep it written down somewhere both of you can find it. A search for IB tutors near me Mumbai will produce a long list of options; the arrangement that lasts a full term is the one where both sides wrote down the same understanding on day one and neither had to remember it.
bullets: Bring the last two marked school assignments with teacher comments
Have the subject guide and this term's assessment calendar ready

faqs.question: Two tutors have quoted for DP Chemistry HL and the two quotes are far apart. What do I actually compare?
faqs.answer: Compare what is inside each quote before you compare the quotes themselves. Ask both tutors the same seven questions: what a session includes, whether marking between sessions is inside the quote or billed separately, whether travel time is charged, what happens if you cancel, what happens if they cancel, how much notice each side gives, and when payment is due and for what period. Write the answers in two columns. Most of the gap between two quotes for the same subject disappears once you can see that one includes marked past papers and a written summary while the other is contact time only. IB home tutor fees in Mumbai only become comparable at that point.

faqs.question: Is marking of past papers between sessions normally included?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and you have to ask, because it is the most common difference between two quotes for identical work. Marking a Diploma Programme Chemistry paper properly against the mark scheme takes a tutor real time outside the session, and tutors handle it in three ways: inside the quote, billed separately, or not offered at all. None of those is dishonest. What causes trouble is discovering in week four that the paper your child sat on Sunday will not be looked at because nobody established who was marking it. Settle it in one sentence before the first session and it never comes up again.

faqs.question: Should we pay for a full term in advance if the tutor asks for it?
faqs.answer: We would not, and we say the same thing to tutors. An advance covering a full term removes your ability to change course cheaply when the match is wrong in week three, and a wrong match in week three happens even with experienced tutors. Ask instead for a short renewable cycle, four sessions at a time, reviewed before it renews. A tutor confident in their own work rarely objects to that, because they expect to be renewed. If a tutor insists on a long advance and will not explain the reason, treat the insistence as information about the arrangement rather than a negotiation to be won.

faqs.question: What cancellation notice should we agree, and does it work both ways?
faqs.answer: Agree the same notice for both sides, in writing, before the first session. A common and fair arrangement is notice by the previous evening for a routine change, with the session rescheduled rather than treated as used, plus an understanding that repeated last-minute cancellations from either direction end the arrangement. The part parents forget is the other direction: what happens when the tutor cancels because a journey across Mumbai failed. If the terms only bind your household, they are not terms. Ask the tutor how many sessions they lost last term and listen to how specifically they answer that.

faqs.question: Our building in Kanjurmarg issues visitor passes only until early evening. Does that affect a 7pm slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth settling before you choose the tutor rather than afterwards. Many Mumbai societies, including towers in Kanjurmarg, Powai and Thane West, require a pass logged in advance for a recurring visitor, and some close the register at a fixed hour. Ask your facility office for a standing weekly entry in the tutor's name once the slot is fixed, and give the tutor the gate's name and number. Tutors lose slots to gate disputes more often than to teaching problems, and ten minutes stuck at a gate twice a week is time the household has already paid for.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who lives in our own society better than a better-matched one in Thane?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, but proximity is worth more than most parents assume. A tutor in the same complex keeps the slot through monsoon evenings, arrives unhurried, and can move a session by an hour without a negotiation. A better-matched specialist in Thane may teach the component more precisely and then lose two sessions in July to Ghodbunder Road. The honest answer depends on the subject. For Mathematics AA HL or a rare Language B, take the specialist and run them online through the monsoon. For MYP Mathematics or IGCSE First Language English, take the neighbour and keep the consistency.

faqs.question: What costs do families forget when planning for IB home tuition in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Three, reliably. Past paper packs, a revision guide and printing, which look small individually and add up across six Diploma Programme subjects. The second weekly session that appears in January or April when deadlines stack, which is the largest single change most households make to what they spend on home tuition. And the younger sibling who watches the arrangement working and wants one too, usually in a different subject with a different tutor and a different quote. Build all three into the plan at the start and exam term stops producing financial surprises on top of academic ones.

faqs.question: Does adding a second session in exam term need a new arrangement?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a new agreement rather than an extension, because that is what it actually is. Agree whether the additional session runs online or at home, which hour it occupies, how many weeks it lasts, and the date it ends. Open-ended additions made in February have a way of surviving until June without anybody deciding to keep them. If the extra session exists to clear a specific Internal Assessment or to prepare for a mock, say that out loud, put an end date against it, and review at the end whether it did what it was added to do.

faqs.question: Can we ask a tutor to put what is included in writing?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a tutor who refuses is telling you something useful early. It does not need to look like a contract. Six lines in a message covers it: session length and slot, what happens between sessions, whether marking and feedback are included, how travel is treated, notice on both sides, and the payment cycle. IB Gram keeps that summary on file for matches it makes, so a question in week eight has a reference point. Most disputes between families and tutors in Mumbai are not about money at all; they are about two different memories of one conversation.

faqs.question: If the tutor cancels at short notice, what should happen?
faqs.answer: The session should be rescheduled rather than treated as used, and that should be agreed before the first class instead of argued about afterwards. Journeys fail in Mumbai for reasons nobody controls: a block on the Western Line, water across the Eastern Express Highway, a signal failure that turns thirty minutes into ninety. A reasonable tutor offers a replacement slot inside the same week or runs that session online. What you are watching for is the pattern rather than the incident. One failed journey in a term is Mumbai; three in a month is a tutor who has accepted a slot they cannot reach.

faqs.question: How do we know when to stop paying for tuition?
faqs.answer: When your child starts a question without being told how to start it, and keeps doing that for several weeks running. That is the exit signal, and it is worth asking every tutor at the introduction what they think it looks like in their subject. Tuition that continues out of habit is the most expensive kind, because it costs money and it also costs the student the experience of working alone before an examination where nobody is sitting beside them. A tutor who tells you in March that you can stop in April has earned the next referral.

A Year 6 Middle Years Programme (MYP) child who needs reading stamina and a Diploma Programme (DP) second-year student with a Physics Internal Assessment (IA) draft due are not the same hire, and a tutor who is excellent at one is often wrong for the other. So the first conversation is short and factual: which programme, which subjects, which two evenings, and whether a parent will be in the flat.

Geography comes next, and in Airoli it comes before credentials. A tutor living near Thane station reaches an Airoli building off the Airoli–Thane–Belapur Road faster than one coming up from Nerul or Vashi. sections.heading: Which IB programme is your child actually in?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs three school-age programmes and they need different tutors. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers the early years and is taught through units of inquiry. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school years and is assessed against published criteria. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the two-year pre-university course with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects, the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the service component. Airoli families send children into all three, often at the same school, and the tutor who suits one will not automatically suit the next.

The practical difference for a parent in Airoli is what the tutor has to be good at. PYP work rewards a tutor who can sit with a child and build reading and number confidence without reaching for worksheets. MYP work rewards someone who can read a criterion strand and show a child what a stronger response looks like against it. DP work rewards subject depth and nothing else; a strong generalist will not rescue an HL Chemistry student in the second year. A request for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need across twelve years of school is really a request for several people over time.

Year groups move, and so does the right tutor. A child who worked happily with the same person through MYP often needs a change at the start of DP1, because the assessment stops being criterion-based classroom work and becomes externally examined papers plus internal assessment. If your child is on a Cambridge pathway instead, our separate Airoli page for that board covers the tiering decision; this page stays with the IB. The pool description we work from reads all IB and IGCSE subjects IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai, which in plain English means twelve years of different pathways rather than one product.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, and the assessments that follow
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision parents in Airoli ask about most, and it is usually made under time pressure in the term before DP1 starts. The IB asks for a subject from each group plus the core, with some taken at Higher Level and the rest at Standard Level. A parent who wants help across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Airoli can cover is normally asking two questions at once: is this combination survivable, and which two subjects will need outside help from the first month rather than from February.

The honest answer is that the combination matters less than the internal assessment load it creates. Every DP subject carries internally assessed work: a scientific investigation in the sciences, an exploration in Mathematics, an oral in a language, a research task in the individuals and societies group. Those pieces do not arrive evenly. They cluster, and they cluster in the same months as the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. An IB home tutor in Airoli who has sat through two DP cycles will tell you where the collision is before it happens rather than after.

Weightings, paper counts and durations change, so take them from the current subject guide for the year your child actually sits, or from the Diploma Programme coordinator at their school, and not from any page like this one. What does not change is the shape of the work: a draft, feedback, one redraft, and a school deadline set well ahead of the board's. Where home tuition earns its keep is in the redraft week, when a tutor sitting beside the student can turn a vague teacher comment into one specific change to the method section.

sections.heading: Ghansoli, Kopar Khairane and Thane West: one Navi Mumbai travel radius

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, each a short drive from the next on the Sion–Panvel Highway and Palm Beach Road, and tutors are matched node to node for a reason. IB home classes in Airoli hold their slot for a full term when the tutor's own flat is inside that arc.

Thane West is the one that surprises people. Airoli is on the Trans-Harbour Line one stop from Thane, so Airoli families are often matched with Thane tutors rather than Navi Mumbai ones, and that is not a compromise. It is the larger pool. Thane has a deeper bench of Diploma Programme subject specialists than the northern Navi Mumbai nodes do, and the train takes minutes. A tutor who lives near Thane station and teaches two Airoli students on the same evening is the most durable arrangement on this corridor, because the travel is already paid for.

Ghansoli and Kopar Khairane matter for a different reason: they are where the second student often is. Tutors build an evening out of two or three stops, and a slot in Airoli that sits next to an existing Ghansoli or Kopar Khairane booking is the one that survives the monsoon, the examination fortnight and the tutor's own commute. A bus that leaves Airoli early and returns late changes everything about scheduling. A DP student off a Nerul or Thane bus is home with homework already waiting, which is why the workable weekday window here starts around half past six and closes by half past eight. Earlier does not exist on school days. Later does not work for a tutor who still has to get back to Thane West. Weekend mornings are the pressure valve and they fill first, so families who book in June hold better slots than families who book in October.

The calendar pressure points repeat every year. The DP May examination session pulls mock examinations into the winter months, and the internal assessment drafts land in the term before, which is when demand for a Diploma Programme subject specialist in Navi Mumbai peaks and the good tutors are already committed. MYP criterion tasks and PYP exhibitions have their own clusters. Ask your school's examinations officer or Diploma Programme coordinator for the actual dates for your child's cohort, put them on a calendar, and book tuition against that calendar rather than against a bad report card.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix for an Airoli family?
paragraphs: For most Airoli families the answer is home tuition for the subject that is actually failing and online for anything else. A tutor in the room is worth more for a child who stops working the moment nobody is watching, and IB home tutoring in Airoli is the default we suggest for DP1 and DP2 students carrying internal assessment deadlines. It is also the version with a travel cost attached, and on this corridor that cost is real rather than notional.

An IB online tutor in Airoli solves the travel problem and creates two others. The first is attention: a fourteen-year-old with a laptop and a closed door is not supervised, and the gain from a scarce specialist can be lost to the drift. The second is workload: handwritten Mathematics and annotated past papers move badly over a screen unless the family has a tablet or a document camera set up. Where online genuinely wins is a rare HL subject with no local teacher, a tutor who has moved away, and the week before a paper when a short review beats a cancelled visit.

Hybrid is what most arrangements become by the second term, and it is worth planning rather than drifting into. One visit a week in the flat for the teaching that needs a shared table, one shorter online check-in for marking and questions. An IB private tutor Airoli families hire through a neighbour usually offers only one of the two. Being clear about which hour is in person and which is on a screen also keeps the fee predictable, because travel is most of what makes a visit cost more than a video call.

sections.heading: What is checked before a tutor rings your bell in Airoli?
paragraphs: Before any name reaches an Airoli family three things are checked: government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and real experience with the board and level in the request. Experience is the one that matters most and is easiest to dress up in a profile, so it is tested by asking the tutor to talk through an internal assessment they have actually supervised and what they did when the student's first draft came back off-topic.

There is work only you can do, and it takes about ten minutes. Ask the tutor which year they last taught the subject and at which level. Ask what they do when a child has not done the homework. Ask for the school name of a current or recent student and listen for hesitation rather than for a name. An IB home tutor in Airoli who has taught DP Mathematics for several cycles will answer all three in plain language. No honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades either.

Access is part of verification in a Navi Mumbai tower. Most buildings here want a name on the gate register and a resident's confirmation before a visitor goes up, and some want a photograph as well. sections.heading: What do IB tuition fees in Airoli depend on?
paragraphs: IB tuition fees in Airoli depend on five things: the board and level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, how long the session runs, and whether the slot is a prime weekday evening or a quieter weekend morning. There is no single rate for this corridor, and anyone quoting one before hearing the subject and the year group is guessing at your situation.

Level does most of the work. A Higher Level DP subject in the second year costs more per hour than MYP support, because the pool of people who can teach it well is small and all of them are busy in the same months. Scarcity does the rest: a common subject has many candidates inside the Airoli radius, while a rarer one may have two or three people across the whole of Thane and Navi Mumbai, and you are effectively bidding for an evening. Travel is the third factor and the one Airoli families can control, because a tutor from Thane West spends less of the evening in transit than one from the island city.

Two things are worth attention in the quote itself. First, ask whether the fee is per session or per hour, and what happens to a ninety-minute session during an examination fortnight. Second, ask how cancellations work, because a tutor who has travelled to Airoli and found nobody home has lost the whole evening. Paying monthly rather than per visit is normal here and makes both sides more reliable. Booking all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Airoli parents want on one timetable costs more than it looks, because it means two or three tutors rather than one.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process, not marks. The homework gets done without a fight, the child can say what the next deadline is, and the tutor's notes name a specific weakness rather than describing what happened in the session. If after four weeks nobody can tell you what the actual gap is, that is the signal to change tutor, and it is a far cheaper decision in September than it is in February with a draft due.

At one term you should see marks move on the kind of task that was failing, and see it in school work rather than only in tuition exercises. A DP1 student who could not finish a paper in the time allowed starts finishing it. An MYP student who kept losing marks on one criterion starts hitting it. Searching for the best IB tutor in Airoli will not shorten this; one term is roughly how long a changed working habit takes to show up in a school report, whoever is teaching.

Over a full examination cycle the honest limits matter. A tutor can close a skills gap, rebuild technique, and make a student calmer and faster under timed conditions. A tutor cannot replace two years of absent coursework in six weeks, cannot sit the paper, and cannot promise a specific grade. We do not guarantee grades, and anyone who does is selling something other than teaching. What we can say is what usually changes and in what order: confidence, then completion, then accuracy, then marks.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Airoli actually do in the first week?
faqs.answer: An IB home tutor in Airoli diagnoses and teaches in that order during the first week, then sends you a written note. Session one starts with the last two pieces of marked work and the teacher's comments, because those show the gap faster than any placement test. The tutor then teaches for most of the hour so your child is not interviewed for sixty minutes. The note afterwards names one specific weakness, such as unfinished papers or thin criterion responses, and sets out what the next three sessions will cover. Week one is not for long-term planning; it is for finding the real problem.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Airoli for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor lives inside the radius. Someone based in Thane West, Ghansoli or Kopar Khairane will hold a 7pm Airoli slot through a full term, because the Trans-Harbour Line and the Airoli–Thane–Belapur Road make it a short trip rather than a project. A tutor coming across the creek from the island city will accept the slot in June and start rescheduling by August. This is exactly why we filter by travel before credentials: a slightly less decorated tutor who arrives every single week beats a better one who arrives most weeks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get past our building gate without a standing pass?
faqs.answer: Usually once, and then it becomes a weekly argument. Most Navi Mumbai societies log visitors and will call the flat before letting anyone up, which is fine for a first visit and tiresome as a routine. Give your security desk the tutor's name, the day and the time in writing at the start, and ask whether the society issues a monthly visitor pass for regular home tuition. faqs.question: Do your tutors live in Airoli itself, or do they come from Thane?
faqs.answer: Both, and Thane supplies more of them. Airoli is on the Trans-Harbour Line one stop from Thane, so Airoli families are often matched with Thane tutors rather than Navi Mumbai ones, particularly for Diploma Programme subjects where the local bench is thin. Tutors living in Airoli, Ghansoli and Kopar Khairane cover middle years and primary work comfortably. For a Higher Level science or Mathematics specialist, expect a Thane West name and a short train or road trip. Either way the tutor sits inside one travel radius, which is what keeps a weekly slot alive past the second month.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Airoli depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on level, subject scarcity, travel distance, session length and slot timing. A second-year Higher Level subject costs more per hour than Middle Years Programme support, because fewer people teach it well and they are busy in the same months. A rare subject costs more again, since you are competing for one of very few free evenings across Thane and Navi Mumbai. Travel shows up in the price, so a tutor from inside the radius is cheaper than one crossing the creek. Ask whether the rate is per hour or per session, and how cancellations are handled, before the first visit.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP student usually need?
faqs.answer: For one subject, two sessions a week during an internal assessment period and one the rest of the time is the usual shape. Two subjects in trouble means two tutors, and that is where timetables break: a DP2 student with school, a Higher Level draft and four tuition hours a week is not going to sleep. Start with the subject costing the most marks, run it for a month, and add the second only once the first is stable. More hours are not the same thing as more learning, and a tired student learns very little in the fourth hour.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP, not DP. Is that the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Often not, and it is better to accept that early than to discover it in March. Middle Years Programme work is assessed against published criteria, so the tutor needs to read a strand and show a child what a stronger response looks like against it. Diploma Programme work needs subject depth and examination technique. Some tutors do both well; most are clearly better at one. For MYP we look for someone who can teach skills and keep a twelve-year-old working, and for DP we look for the subject specialist. Ask which level the tutor last taught and in which year.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three weeks?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we arrange a replacement without arguing about it. Three or four weeks is the right point to judge, and the test is not whether your child enjoys the sessions but whether anyone can name the actual gap and the plan for closing it. If the notes are vague, the homework is still a fight, or the tutor keeps rescheduling, that is enough. Replacement means a fresh shortlist from the same Airoli radius, carrying the diagnosis you already have, so the new tutor does not start from zero. Changing once is normal; changing three times means the brief is wrong.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for an IB student in Navi Mumbai?
faqs.answer: It works well for some things and badly for others. Online is the right answer for a scarce Higher Level subject with no teacher inside the Airoli radius, for a tutor who has moved away, and for a short review in an examination week when a cancelled visit would be worse. It works badly for a student who needs someone in the room to stay on task, and for handwritten Mathematics without a tablet or document camera. Most Navi Mumbai families settle on one visit and one online check-in a week, which is a sensible arrangement rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: What should we do about the monsoon and missed evening sessions?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in June, before you need it. The monsoon will take out evenings on this corridor, and the fair arrangement is a switch to an online session at the same hour rather than a cancellation, with a make-up slot at the weekend if the subject has a deadline coming. Say explicitly who decides and by what time: a message by five o'clock keeps everyone honest. Tutors travelling to Airoli from Thane West lose an entire evening to a late cancellation, so a written rule protects the arrangement far better than goodwill does.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Maths and Chemistry, or do we need two?
faqs.answer: At Middle Years Programme level one tutor can often do both; at Diploma Programme Higher Level, assume two. The subjects diverge in the second year, when the Mathematics exploration and the Chemistry investigation need different kinds of supervision and different marking habits. A tutor who claims both at Higher Level may well be fine, so ask which one they taught most recently and which internal assessments they have actually supervised. If the answer is thin on one side, split the hours. Two specialists for one hour each usually beats one generalist for two hours.

sections.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: which rung of the IB ladder is your child on?
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) is three programmes stacked on each other, not one course, and a parent on Altamount Road who says my daughter does IB could mean any of them. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) runs through the early years and closes with an exhibition in the final year. The Middle Years Programme (MYP) covers the middle school span, assesses against published criteria rather than a single terminal paper, and ends in a personal project that most students underestimate. The Diploma Programme (DP) is the last two years: six subjects split between Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the creativity, activity, service strand.

Each rung needs a different kind of help in the room. PYP work rewards a tutor who can build reading stamina and number sense without turning an inquiry unit into a worksheet. MYP work rewards criterion literacy, because a child who writes well and still scores in the middle band is usually missing a command term, not the content. DP work rewards a specialist. The IB Gram directory is deliberately broad, and you will see it listed as a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents can draw on, but a broad listing is not how a match is made. The tutor who comes to your flat teaches one or two subjects at one or two levels.

Do not take level loadings, paper counts, component weights or submission dates from a page like this one, including this one. The IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle, and the version your child is registered against is the only one that matters. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds it. If your child is in the Years 9 to 11 band on Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel rather than the IB, the IGCSE home tutor in Altamount Road page covers that lane properly and this one does not.

sections.heading: Subject choice across the IB, and the internal assessments each one carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is the decision that quietly sets the next two years, and it is made in a fortnight in DP1. Every Diploma Programme subject carries an internally assessed component alongside its examinations, and those components are where tutoring earns its keep, because they are drafted, marked by the school and moderated externally. A sciences student produces an individual investigation with its own research question and data. A mathematics student produces an exploration. A language student produces oral and written work. The skills are not interchangeable: a tutor who is excellent at past-paper technique is not automatically useful on a research question.

Work through a real case. A DP1 student at Aditya Birla World Academy takes HL Chemistry and HL Mathematics with SL Economics, and arrives in October with an acceptable school report and a vague unease. The diagnostic session shows the Chemistry problem is not content at all but experimental design, because she has never had to choose her own variables. The Mathematics problem is the opposite: fluent manipulation, no idea what makes an exploration question answerable. That is two different tutors, or one tutor with an honest admission about which half she is weaker on, and it is the sort of thing a phone call before the first visit surfaces.

Name the papers and the skills, then take structure from the current guide.

paragraphs: Families on this stretch mostly send children to a small set of South Mumbai schools, and the two closest reference points are Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo and Activity High School on Peddar Road. Their calendars, not the examination session, are what actually govern your evenings. The Mumbai school year opens in June, so the first reporting cycle lands in the monsoon, the heavy internal deadlines cluster from late in the calendar year into the new one, and the May examination session sits at the far end of a long second term. A tutor who does not know that rhythm will plan backwards from the wrong date.

The pressure points are predictable enough to put in a diary. September to November is where DP2 Internal Assessment drafts and the Extended Essay collide, and where a child who has been coasting since June is found out. January and February bring mock examinations and the last realistic window to change technique before the real session. March and April are consolidation and nerves, not new content. For MYP years, the personal project deadline and the final criterion-marked tasks are the two dates worth protecting, and they rarely fall where a parent assumes they will.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Aditya Birla World Academy, Activity High School, or any other school named anywhere on this page; schools are listed here because they are the local context a tutor has to work inside. And a good home tutor works with the school rather than around it. If the school has set a Theory of Knowledge essay title and a presentation date, the tutor's job is to get your child through both on the school's terms, not to run a parallel syllabus in your dining room.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix for a DP student on Altamount Road
paragraphs: Start with the default, because for most families here it is the right one. IB home tuition in Altamount Road means a tutor in the flat, at a table, with the lab book and the folder physically open, and that matters more for the IB than for a syllabus assessed only by examination. Internal Assessment work is iterative. Someone has to see the actual draft, the actual data table and the actual teacher comments, and home classes make that routine instead of an attachment someone forgot to send. In-apartment lessons also survive a bad week in a way that a screen does not.

Online has two honest uses rather than one. The first is scarcity: if your child needs HL Further Mathematics, a less commonly taught language, or a specific Theory of Knowledge examiner's eye, an IB online tutor in Altamount Road may simply be better than the nearest available body, and an hour saved on Peddar Road is an hour of teaching. The second is the examination run-in, when a sixty-minute slot three times a week is more useful than ninety minutes once, and travel makes the three impossible. The cost is real: attention is harder to hold, written work needs scanning, and a tired DP2 student hides more easily on a video call.

Hybrid is what most of our island families settle into by the second term, and it is worth planning rather than drifting into. One home visit a week carries the diagnosis, the marking and the difficult conversation. One or two short online sessions carry drill, past-paper walkthroughs and draft feedback. Review the split at every deadline cluster rather than once a year, because a child who needed two home sessions a week in October may need one in March, and a family paying for travel they no longer need is the most common quiet waste in this arrangement.

paragraphs: Every IB home tutor listed with IB Gram has been through the same checks before a parent on Altamount Road ever sees a name: government identity proof, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, and the specific IB experience asserted, which is the one most often overstated. Having taught a subject is not having taught it at Higher Level. Having taught at Higher Level is not having supervised Internal Assessment work that went through moderation. We ask which programme, which level and which components, and a tutor who cannot answer precisely does not get shortlisted for a Diploma Programme request.

Then there is the part only you can do, and it takes one phone call. Ask which board and which level the tutor taught most recently, and in which year. Ask what they would do in the first three sessions with your child's specific problem, and listen for whether the answer is about your child or about their method. Ask how they handle a draft the school has already marked down. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, or who answers a question about assessment structure with confidence instead of pointing you at the current guide.

Building clearance is the last layer and the one families here care about most. A tutor is registered with the gate desk under their own name with the standing slot recorded, so entry is routine from the second week rather than renegotiated. Tutors are briefed that a flat is a home and not a classroom: shoes, phones, the room they are given and the hour they leave. If a tutor's conduct inside your building is a problem, that is grounds for a replacement on its own, independent of whether the teaching was any good.

Second, stop looking for the best IB tutor in Altamount Road in the abstract. sections.heading: What home tuition should change by week four, and what it cannot
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at marks. Look for three things instead: your child can say what the tutor is working on without being prompted, the homework pattern has changed, and the tutor has told you something about your child's work that the school had not. Home tuition that has not produced those three signals in a month is not working, whatever the atmosphere in the room is like. Marks at four weeks are mostly noise, because the assessments in that window were set before anyone arrived and measure the term before this one.

At one term, you should see movement in the specific component you hired for. A sciences student who could not design an investigation should have a research question the school has accepted. A mathematics student should have an exploration that is answerable. An essay subject should show structural change, usually visible in the first paragraph. If the component that drove you to find a tutor looks the same in February as it did in October, raise it directly and change something, because a second term of the same arrangement rarely produces a different result.

At one examination cycle, the honest statement is this: IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no tutor can, because the paper, the moderator and the day are outside everybody's control. What tutoring reliably changes is the quality and timeliness of the work your child submits, and the margin of error on examination day. Progress is also not linear across the Diploma Programme. Most DP2 students get worse before they get better when technique changes, which is uncomfortable in November and the reason February exists.

And the two evening windows that genuinely work, allowing for traffic on Peddar Road rather than the time you would prefer.

Add one Altamount Road specific item: the name and number of your building's gate desk or society office, and whatever they require for a recurring visitor. That single detail is the difference between a first lesson that starts at seven and one that starts at twenty past. Tutors here are briefed on society procedure before the first visit, but nobody can register with a desk that has not been identified, and the towers along this road do not all run the same protocol.

The first session is diagnosis rather than teaching, and it is worth telling your child that in advance so they do not treat it as a test. The tutor works through the current unit, the last marked piece, and the component that is actually failing, then gives you a plain assessment of what can and cannot be fixed before the next deadline. If that assessment and the phone call before it do not match, say so immediately. Starting IB home tuition in Altamount Road on a clear diagnosis is worth more than starting it a week earlier on a vague one.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Altamount Road do in the very first session?
faqs.answer: Diagnose, not teach. The first visit goes through the current unit, the last marked piece of work with the teacher's comments, and the specific component that is going wrong, then produces a plain statement of what can realistically be fixed before your next deadline. A tutor who opens the first session by teaching chapter one has skipped the only step that saves a term. You should receive a short plan afterwards naming the component, the order of work, and what your child is expected to do between sessions. If that plan contradicts what you were told on the phone, raise it immediately.

faqs.question: Can a tutor be cleared at the building gate for a standing weekly evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is arranged before the first visit rather than after it. The tutor's name, identity proof and the fixed weekly slot are sent to your building's gate desk or society office so entry becomes routine from the second week. This matters more on Altamount Road than in most of Mumbai, because the towers along this short stretch each run their own visitor protocol and the service lift is busiest at exactly seven in the evening. A tutor who has not been registered can lose fifteen minutes of a sixty-minute slot at the desk, which you are paying for.

faqs.question: Does an evening tutor from Tardeo reach Altamount Road faster than one from the suburbs?
faqs.answer: Almost always, and the gap is bigger than the map suggests. South Mumbai is short in distance but slow: the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals can absorb most of an hour in the evening peak, so a tutor already inside the island from Tardeo, Cumballa Hill or Peddar Road arrives predictably while one travelling down from the Western Suburbs arrives late once a fortnight and then renegotiates the slot. That is why IB Gram matches within the island for weekday evening lessons and treats a suburban match as an online or weekend arrangement instead.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a home tutor for in South Mumbai?
faqs.answer: The scarce ones are the upper end of mathematics, the less commonly taught languages, and specialist Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision. Higher Level sciences are findable on the island; a tutor who has actually supervised moderated Internal Assessment work in those sciences is harder. For the genuinely scarce requests, the realistic answer is often an online specialist rather than a weaker local match, because proximity does not help a child whose problem is a research question nobody nearby has supervised. Ask for the component, and accept a screen when the component demands it.

faqs.question: Does one tutor stay with a child from MYP into the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it should be a deliberate decision rather than inertia. Continuity is genuinely valuable through the Middle Years Programme, where criterion literacy and writing habits build slowly. The move into DP1 changes the job, because Higher Level content and Internal Assessment supervision need subject depth that a strong generalist may not have. The honest pattern is continuity until subject choice is made, then a review: keep the tutor where the subject matches their depth, and add or switch where it does not. A tutor who refuses to discuss that review is telling you something.

faqs.question: How do IB tuition fees in Altamount Road change between Standard Level and Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Higher Level work costs more, and the reason is supply rather than hours. Fewer tutors can teach HL content properly and fewer still have supervised Internal Assessment work through moderation, so the pool is smaller and prices accordingly. Subject scarcity moves the figure further than the level does, and travel distance and session frequency move it again. We do not publish a rate card because any number printed on a page is out of date and ignores your address, your subject and the month you are starting in. Ask two or three tutors directly once you know the component you need.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell IB Gram and a different tutor is shortlisted, without an argument about who was at fault. Three sessions is the right moment to judge: enough for the diagnosis to be visible, not enough to have lost a term. Fit failures are usually structural rather than personal, such as a tutor strong on examination technique matched to a child whose problem is a research question. Say what specifically did not work, because that detail makes the second match better. Building clearance for a replacement tutor is handled the same way as the first, and the standing slot usually survives the change.

faqs.question: Can online lessons replace home classes during the May examination session?
faqs.answer: They can, and in the final weeks they often should. Short, frequent sessions beat long weekly ones in the run-in, and three thirty-minute online slots are achievable in a week where three home visits across Mumbai traffic are not. The trade-off is supervision: scanned work loses detail, and a tired student hides more easily on a screen. The arrangement that works best keeps one home visit a week for marking and the difficult conversation, and moves the drill online. Decide this in February, not in the week before the first paper.

faqs.question: Our DP2 child has an Internal Assessment draft and a Theory of Knowledge essay due in the same fortnight. What can a tutor realistically do?
faqs.answer: Sequence the work and protect one of the two. A tutor cannot write either piece and should not try, but can get the Internal Assessment to a state where the school's feedback is useful, and reduce the Theory of Knowledge essay to a defensible structure with a clear knowledge question. That collision is normal between September and November for Diploma Programme students across Mumbai, and the families who come through it well are the ones who fixed the order of work three weeks earlier. The realistic aim is both pieces submitted on time and defensible, not both polished.

faqs.question: Do parents here search for IB tutors near me in Altamount Road, or go by word of mouth?
faqs.answer: Both, and the two produce different problems. Word of mouth on this road is strong and tends to recycle the same handful of names regardless of subject, which is how a child ends up with a capable tutor in the wrong component. A search gives you a wider pool and no filtering at all. Use both: take the recommendation, then ask it the same specific questions you would ask a stranger about level, component and recent board experience. A name that was right for a neighbour's MYP child may be wrong for your DP2 one.

faqs.question: Is there a best IB tutor in Altamount Road, and how would we tell?
faqs.answer: No, and the question is worth replacing. There is no single best IB tutor in Altamount Road, only the tutor whose subject, level and free evening match the component your child is actually failing. The test is not reputation but the first three sessions: has the diagnosis been specific, has the homework pattern changed, and has the tutor told you something the school report did not. Those three signals identify a good match faster than any ranking, and IB Gram does not publish rankings because the ordering would change with every subject and address.

sections.heading: How we build an IB home tutor shortlist for Andheri East
paragraphs: The brief matters more than the subject name. A parent writes to say their daughter is in Diploma Programme year one (DP1), takes Higher Level (HL) Chemistry and Standard Level (SL) Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and has an Internal Assessment (IA) draft she has rewritten twice without her teacher being satisfied. That paragraph already rules out most of the pool, because strong HL Chemistry and strong SL Mathematics almost never sit in the same person. The brief we cannot do much with is the one that says IB tuition, evenings, flexible.

So the sequence is deliberately boring. 1. You send the year group, each subject with its level, the school, and the two or three things actually going wrong. 2. We read that against tutors who already work the Andheri East–Western Express Highway / JVLR corridor and filter on subject and level first, location second. 3. You receive two or three profiles that state the board they teach, the levels they hold, and what they decline to take on. 4. You speak to whichever one you prefer on a free discovery call, and an IB home tutor in Andheri East starts lessons only after you say yes.

Location comes second because an unsuitable tutor who lives ten minutes away is still unsuitable in week six. It comes second, not last, because a standing weekly slot that requires someone to cross the city at 6pm will quietly collapse by the end of the term. The compromise that holds here is a tutor already oriented to this corridor, which is a larger group than most parents expect for reasons the coverage section explains.

When a combination is genuinely scarce, we say so rather than sending a near-miss. HL Chemistry plus HL Mathematics in the same tutor, or a Group 2 language at HL, can take longer to fill than a week. A slower honest match beats a fast one you replace in a month, and replacing a tutor costs your child the two or three weeks it takes a new person to learn how she thinks.
